title: Rational and real Fourier observations
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, let $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $x$ be a point of that cube. The rational observation formed from the label $f(x)$ and the product of the coordinates indexed by $S$, when regarded as a real number, equals the real-valued Fourier observation of $f$ at $x$ for $S$.
hypotheses_covered: A sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
A point $x$ in the sign cube
